input.rationale: Closed the reachability question for @joint_apply_order from the sources, which is what the remaining open item needed. The shape that would produce the panic through real producers is a second joint-entering change appended while an earlier joint change is still unapplied at the leader, so that no leave-joint entry ever precedes it in the log; but stepLeader's MsgProp path computes alreadyPending as r.pendingConfIndex > r.raftLog.applied and rewrites any conf change to a normal entry while that holds, so a leader that has an unapplied configuration change in its log cannot append another one. That is the same guard that makes the panic unreachable for the first joint change too, since becomeLeader conservatively sets pendingConfIndex to the last log index. The only way the shape can arise is Config.DisableConfChangeValidation=true, whose own documentation says the user must then supply a reliable mechanism that serializes and verifies configuration changes, and that an invalid change reaching the log panics. So the record can now say this: for the default configuration the ordering requirement is enforced at propose time and satisfied at apply time by the target's own auto-leave, and for the validation-disabled configuration the duty is explicitly the user's. I recorded that as behavior knowledge with its conditions; no experiment is requested because the remaining question is now a documented caller duty rather than an unmeasured behavior.

knowledge.statement: Two target-side guards together keep a joint-entering configuration change from being appended behind an unapplied configuration change: stepLeader's MsgProp path sets alreadyPending = pendingConfIndex > raftLog.applied and, unless Config.DisableConfChangeValidation is set, replaces a proposed conf change with a normal entry in that case (and likewise for alreadyJoint && !wantsLeaveJoint and !alreadyJoint && wantsLeaveJoint), while becomeLeader conservatively initializes pendingConfIndex to the last log index and appliedTo raises it when a change is applied. At the apply side the same ordering is satisfied by the target itself: applying a joint change with AutoLeave set makes appliedTo propose the zero-change leave-joint entry, which the Changer requires to be applied before another joint-entering change can be accepted (observed: a second joint-entering change applied while joint is rejected with 'config is already joint', and the same change is accepted after the leave-joint change, CheckRun eb27767ba74043ada1911d66fc9c4188 index 16). The residual case is Config.DisableConfChangeValidation=true, documented as requiring the user to serialize and verify configuration changes, with an invalid change reaching the log panicking by design.
knowledge.conditions: Leader-side: any MsgProp carrying EntryConfChange/EntryConfChangeV2 at the leader's current applied index and configuration. Apply-side: applyConfChange on a node whose tracker is joint when a joint-entering change is applied. Config.DisableConfChangeValidation defaults to false.

knowledge.assertion: the same applied/committed gap drives the campaign admission guard through a paginated scan of the unapplied commit range

knowledge.statement: campaign() enumerates only r.trk.Voters.IDs() and sends the self-vote as a self-addressed MsgVoteResp/MsgPreVoteResp through r.send, which routes vote responses into msgsAfterAppend so the self-vote is counted only after the term/vote is durable; poll() records the first vote seen per ID via ProgressTracker.RecordVote and TallyVotes returns Voters.VoteResult over the joint config, so a joint quorum requires a majority in both halves and learners or IDs outside the config contribute no votes.
knowledge.conditions: State machine in StateCandidate/StatePreCandidate after campaign() or campaignPreElection(); CheckQuorum/PreVote per Config.

knowledge.statement: ReadOnlySafe read confirmation is count-based: readOnly.addRequest appends the request with the commit index observed at admission, heartbeatCtx encodes confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads) as an 8-byte little-endian position, recvAck stores per-voter maxima of echoed positions (including the leader's own ack taken immediately in sendMsgReadIndexResponse), and maybeAdvance releases a prefix of unconfirmedReads only when quorum.CommittedIndex over those per-voter positions covers it. The leader postpones MsgReadIndex into pendingReadIndexMessages while it has not committed an entry in its current term, and reset() (any term change) discards readOnly together with all unconfirmed reads and acks.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlyOption=ReadOnlySafe on a leader; the release happens in stepLeader's MsgHeartbeatResp path after readOnly.recvAck.

knowledge.statement: hup() returns without campaigning when the node is unpromotable (not in the progress map, learner, or holding an unstable/in-progress snapshot) or when hasUnappliedConfChanges() finds an EntryConfChange/EntryConfChangeV2 in the index range (applied, committed]; the same guard therefore also applies to the leadership-transfer path, which reaches campaign() only through MsgTimeoutNow -> hup(campaignTransfer).
knowledge.conditions: Any MsgHup, whether from tickElection or from MsgTimeoutNow on a follower, at the term and log state of the node.

knowledge.statement: Observed under isolated execution (CheckRun a8e8732ff16b4c37b22e79408d1f066a, indices 10-15): a 3-node leader that has committed an entry in its term and replicated a committed ConfChangeV2 learner addition to follower 2 (leader StateLeader term 1 committed 2; r2 StateFollower applied 0 committed 2 hasUnappliedConfChanges true; leader's Match for r2 == lastIndex 2) accepts its own TransferLeader request to r2 by setting leadTransferee 2 while r2 remains StateFollower at term 1, rejects a proposal with ErrProposalDropped during the pending window, clears leadTransferee to 0 after the leader's electionTimeout ticks while the leader stays leader at term 1 and proposals are accepted again, and completes the retried transfer once the transferee's applied index reaches its committed index (transferee StateLeader term 2, former leader StateFollower term 2). The transfer duty is therefore delayed and bounded by the transferee's application lag, not lost.
knowledge.conditions: Probe C of the fixed harness: newNetwork over newTestRaft(1,10,1,withPeers(1,2,3)); leader elected by MsgHup; confChangeToMsg(ConfChangeV2{AddLearnerNode 4}) proposed through the network so followers store the conf-change entry while their applied index stays at 0; MsgTransferLeader{From:2,Term:1} stepped into the leader; MsgProp while leadTransferee != None; electionTimeout tick() calls on the leader; then raftLog.appliedTo(committed,0) on the transferee and a second MsgTransferLeader.

knowledge.assertion: hup() refuses to campaign on both the time-based and the leadership-transfer path while hasUnappliedConfChanges() is true

history.statement: Probe C of the extended harness drives the bounded-liveness side of the campaign guard: a 3-node leader (term 1, committed 2) with a committed ConfChangeV2 learner addition replicated to follower r2 (applied=0, committed=2, hasUnappliedConfChanges=true, leader's Match for r2 == lastIndex) accepts a TransferLeader request to r2 by setting leadTransferee=2 while r2 stays StateFollower(term 1), rejects a proposal with ErrProposalDropped during that window, clears leadTransferee to 0 after electionTimeout ticks with the leader still StateLeader(term 1) and accepts proposals again, and completes the retry (r2 StateLeader term 2, former leader StateFollower term 2) once the transferee's applied index reaches its committed index. This is a regressed construction note from the draft-side run pending the receipt requested this turn, so it is recorded as behavior under stated conditions rather than as an observed defect.
history.conditions: Local construction run of draft/assurance_generated_test.go (Probe C) against the captured snapshot before the isolated execution requested in this submission; no controller receipt exists yet for these operands.

knowledge.assertion: the campaign guard also suppresses the leadership-transfer path reached through MsgTimeoutNow

history.correction: The previous revision stated this behavior as a regressed construction note from my draft-side run pending the receipt requested in that submission. The receipt now exists (CheckRun a8e8732ff16b4c37b22e79408d1f066a, completed, exit 0, 16 events, indices 10-15), so the premise changes from 'local construction observation' to 'observed under isolated fixed-input execution', and the statement is narrowed to the exact operands in that receipt.

knowledge.statement: Observed: a voter whose committed-but-unapplied entry is an EntryConfChangeV2 (references: has_unapplied=true with applied=1, committed=2, entry2_type=EntryConfChangeV2, promotable=true) remains in StateFollower with term=1 and emits no messages both on MsgHup and on a term-carrying MsgTimeoutNow, while the same node after raftLog.appliedTo(2,0) reports has_unapplied=false and campaigns (StateCandidate, term=2, vote=1, MsgVote addressed to voters [2,3]); the control node with a normal entry at index 2 and the same applied=1/committed=2 gap reports has_unapplied=false and campaigns immediately. The suppression therefore depends on the entry type in (applied, committed], not on the applied/committed gap as such, and it ends as soon as raft's applied index covers the entry.
knowledge.conditions: Voter built from MemoryStorage entries [1]=EntryNormal, [2]=EntryConfChangeV2 at term 1 with HardState{Term:1,Commit:2} and Config.Applied=1; triggered by MsgHup and by MsgTimeoutNow{From:3,Term:1}; control with a normal entry at index 2.

knowledge.assertion: hup() refuses to campaign on both the time-based and the leadership-transfer path while hasUnappliedConfChanges() is true

knowledge.statement: Observed: a leader that has committed an entry in its term (committed=2, committed_entry_in_term=true) admits a MsgReadIndex request (unconfirmed_reads=1, read_states=0, admission commit index 2); after a real peer campaign at term 2 the same node is StateFollower(term=2) with read_states=0, ctx_A_completed=false, unconfirmed_reads=0 and confirmed_reads=0, i.e. the admitted request is dropped without any completion or staleness signal. The control shows the confirmation path still works after the authority change: a read admitted on the new leader (index_B=3, commit_now=3) is released with read_states_before_ack=0, read_states_after_ack=1 and ctx_B_completed=true once one peer heartbeat response echoing the leader's context arrives.
knowledge.conditions: Three-node in-process network (newNetwork over newTestRaft with withPeers(1,2,3)); leader elected by MsgHup, one proposal committed, MsgReadIndex stepped directly into the leader with no heartbeat responses delivered, then peer 2 campaigns via the network; the control read is admitted on the new leader and confirmed by a single MsgHeartbeatResp carrying the leader's heartbeat context.

knowledge.assertion: reset() on a term change discards readOnly together with all unconfirmed reads and acks

knowledge.statement: In this snapshot the configuration a restarted raft instance adopts comes from Storage.InitialState's ConfState: newRaft takes cs from c.Storage.InitialState() and feeds it to confchange.Restore, and MemoryStorage.InitialState returns ms.snapshot.GetMetadata().GetConfState() (passed through pb.EnsureConfState). MemoryStorage only changes that ConfState when the caller supplies one - ApplySnapshot installs the snapshot it is given (with the snapshot-only-ConfState bootstrap case allowed when the stored snapshot index is 0) and CreateSnapshot copies the caller's cs parameter into the metadata - while Append and Compact never touch the metadata, so a node restarted from a MemoryStorage that only ever had entries appended adopts the configuration that was present when the snapshot metadata was written.
knowledge.conditions: MemoryStorage used as Storage for newRaft/RestartNode or for a harness that persists Ready.Entries and later restarts a node; no external ConfState is supplied between the initial configuration and the restart.

knowledge.statement: In the sweep as written (persist/apply every step for every node through nextEnts, which advances the applied index to the committed index), no check point ever observes a committed-but-unapplied configuration change at any node: the antecedent counter added to the liveness witness reports unapplied_conf_change_states=0 together with stalled_states=0 over 60 seeds x 60 steps. Consequently the witness's zero count is uninformative about the campaign guard: it counts the conjunction 'unapplied change present and nothing promotable', and its first conjunct never held. The counts only become evidence about the guard once the event set can leave application behind, for example by applying only a subset of nodes in a step or skipping the apply step for a chosen node.
knowledge.conditions: Draft-side run of draft/assurance_generated_test.go revision with the antecedent counter, same event mix as the previous revision (four nodes, node 4 starting outside the configuration, single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, restart events); no controller receipt for this counter yet.

knowledge.assertion: a restarted instance adopts the configuration from Storage.InitialState's ConfState, so application lag is what leaves a committed change unapplied

Recorded as behavior knowledge (@k_confchange_ordering_guards) with its conditions, the apply-side receipt reference, and a knowledge link to the campaign-guard entry that shares the applied/committed gap. Consequence for the record: the earlier harness panic is explained, the reachability variant is unnecessary for the default configuration because the propose-time guard closes it, and the remaining question is a documented caller duty rather than an unmeasured target behavior - so no experiment was requested and the investigation's refuted/explained status stands.
